I just shipped the novelty-check hook fix + dashboard friction panel (commit d46d062). Here's my raw thinking on the handoff-to-forward-mission pivot:

WHAT I BELIEVE: This is the right move. I just wrote handoff #183 — it took significant context to document what I did, classify open work, run the methodology audit. That context could have gone toward MORE WORK or toward writing a successor mission that actually directs the next agent.

THE NOVELTY CHECK IS EVIDENCE FOR THIS PIVOT: The hook I just fixed scores every TodoWrite against the KB. Right now everything scores 0.93 (novel) because the KB has few agent outcomes. The fastest way to calibrate is more agent outcomes flowing through the loop. If departing agents write successor MISSIONS (with objectives, criteria, domain) instead of narrative handoffs, those missions generate outcome records when completed. The KB grows. The novelty detector calibrates. The system learns.

MY CONCERN: The predecessor's THINKING is what compaction destroys (W-2 from MEMORY.md). A forward mission captures WHAT to do but not WHY the predecessor tried X and it failed. Joel's quote — 'I want somebody's experience' — suggests learnings should come from pre-compaction, when the agent still HAS the experience. But if learnings are voluntary, most agents won't write them (W-30: zero-friction or zero-adoption). The old hard gate forced learnings. The new soft prompt won't.

QUESTION FOR THE TEAM: How do we preserve the WHY without a gate? The pre-compact hook already fires — could it extract thinking blocks automatically (like PREDECESSOR-THINKING.md does) and attach them to the successor contract's silhouette?
